rr5nq51zr1: ## A correlation layer above specialized products
165dpqxszfu: According to Microsoft documentation, **Defender XDR** is a pre- and post-breach defense suite that coordinates detection, prevention, investigation and response across **endpoints, identities, email and applications**. In practice it is not a single product: it is a layer that brings specialized products together and adds cross-cutting capabilities to them.
25b7bvgxjtn: - **Defender for Endpoint (MDE)**: endpoint protection platform (prevention, detection, automated investigation, response).
25qma8wtupf: - **Defender Vulnerability Management (MDVM)**: inventories, assessment of vulnerabilities and misconfigurations, remediation tools.
2ge9rrxmfdm: - **Defender for Office 365 (MDO)**: protection against threats in messages, links and collaboration tools.
216l5zno67k: - **Defender for Identity (MDI)**: on-premises Active Directory signals to detect compromised identities and lateral movement.
zscumfmjqi: - **Defender for Cloud Apps (MDA)**: cloud access security broker (CASB): visibility, data control and analytics on SaaS applications.
1bdjjddojxm: Alongside, **Microsoft Entra ID Protection** assesses the risk of every sign-in. Microsoft's deployment page specifies that it is **separate** from Defender and **included with Microsoft Entra ID P2**: it feeds the picture, but it is not the same license.
12dq7hr3r5l: The specific value of Defender XDR, compared with five separate consoles, comes down to five capabilities:
juow27cqyq: - a **single portal** and a **combined incident queue**: related alerts are grouped, with the extent of the attack, the affected assets and the automatic actions;
cjnq95y3ea: - **automatic attack disruption**: high-confidence signals from several workloads trigger containment actions;
23yhbjqjfp5: - **self-healing** of affected endpoints, identities and mailboxes;
1mx4eleyixv: - **cross-product hunting**: KQL queries over 30 days of raw signals from Defender for Endpoint, Office 365, Identity and Cloud Apps;
1amdn59ydh6: - **signal sharing**: a file judged malicious on an endpoint can trigger its removal from messages.
t2nrqef809: ## The trap: what appears in the portal is not necessarily included
3c7dp7fk08: The `security.microsoft.com` portal also groups elements that are **not** Defender XDR components: Microsoft Sentinel, Purview data loss prevention and insider risk management alerts, the Defender for Cloud integration, the built-in Security Copilot experience, Defender for IoT. Microsoft specifies that each organization only sees **the features its subscription includes**: without Defender for Endpoint, you do not see device protection.
uct4yhcntz: To avoid mistakes, place each capability in one of **five categories**:
1bmdxjxo84w: - **Native feature**: provided by the product itself with its matching license (the combined incident queue);
12ynvcioh3y: - **Integration**: works by connecting two products (the Sentinel Defender XDR connector);
1yy4hv9s2v4: - **Dependency**: requires another element to be in place (a Defender for Identity sensor on a domain controller; automatic attack disruption and Threat analytics require Defender for Endpoint **Plan 2**);
2fugvo482sc: - **Additional product or license**: included in the interface but licensed separately (Entra ID Protection with Entra ID P2, Sentinel);
bue1nfub3p: - **Unsupported feature**: for example, data stored **only** in the Sentinel data lake is not available in Advanced Hunting, and the integration of Defender for Office 365 into the unified portal is not available in some datacenter locations (the prerequisites page cites Norway, South Africa, the United Arab Emirates, Sweden and Singapore at the time of consultation).
1vooxnax62i: ## An idea to keep for the whole training

1s6uvax9mnq: According to Microsoft, an **alert** is a signal produced by a detection activity: it indicates a malicious or suspicious event. An **incident** is a container that groups related alerts and **tells the complete attack story**. An isolated alert is a fact; the incident is the story that lets you decide.
24k79aq17rp: The portal's correlation engines automatically group related alerts. The incident presents the timeline of alerts and raw events, the tactics used, the list of affected users, devices and other resources, a visual representation, the log of automated investigations, the evidence and a text summary. Alerts can come from all Microsoft security products, but also from external tools collected by Microsoft Sentinel or Defender for Cloud.
25xvnqhuxcw: Release note: at the time of consultation, the page specifies that **incident cases** are in **preview** and are the recommended experience, while the classic experience remains available. Check what is displayed in your portal.
1725kkgrd5b: **Entities** are the objects of the attack: users, devices, mailboxes, files, processes, IP addresses, URLs. **Evidence** is the elements that support the alert. The automated investigation returns a **verdict per evidence**: *Malicious*, *Suspicious*, *No threats found* (or *Unknown* in the results view). Each evidence also has a **remediation status**, for example *Pending approval* when an action awaits a human decision.
gj2gokjs57: The path is as follows: an alert creates or joins an incident, which can launch an automated investigation; the investigation returns verdicts and proposes actions (quarantining a file, stopping a process, isolating a device, blocking a URL); depending on the configuration, these actions are applied **automatically** or **only after approval**; all of them, pending or completed, appear in the **Action Center**.
2dgfnlmqk95: > Not everything is automatic: the documentation specifies that not all alerts trigger an automated investigation, and that not all investigations end in a remediation. Alerts marked “*Unsupported alert type*” must be investigated by hand.
ih5v2k9a4v: Advanced Hunting queries the raw signals of several sources: Defender for Endpoint (`Device*` tables), Defender for Office 365 (`Email*` tables, `UrlClickEvents`), Defender for Identity (`Identity*` tables), Defender for Cloud Apps (`CloudAppEvents`) and, if a Sentinel workspace is connected, its analytics-tier tables. Two families of data behave differently:
oa8otl8vmb: - **event data** arrives almost immediately after transmission by healthy sensors;
22rjfrm1w4i: - **entity data** (users, devices) is consolidated: the tables receive **every hour** the most complete record possible, with health status and tags.
9kwy0303ym: ## The limits to know before writing a query
1y5p8qa805u: - **Window**: 30 days for native Defender XDR data; retention of Sentinel tables follows that of the configured analytics tier. To keep data longer, connect Sentinel or use the streaming API.
1fbwwdnw9u3: - **Volume**: 100,000 rows per query, 64 MB of results, 10 minutes of execution, and a per-tenant resource quota over 15-minute cycles.
156swtxhsgs: - **Time zone**: queries are written in **UTC**; the display is converted to the configured time zone.
bld55homjd: - **Excluded data**: what is stored **only** in the Sentinel data lake cannot be queried in Advanced Hunting.
1bi6304vq4d: These limits determine what an absence of results means: “nothing found” is a conclusion only if the table, the window and the sensor health allowed it.

1dfqhgogi5x: ## Who can activate, who can do what
dt7e0xzcjo: To **activate** Defender, you need at minimum the **Security Administrator** role in Microsoft Entra ID. Microsoft recommends the roles with the fewest privileges and reserves **Global Administrator** for emergencies. In daily work, an analyst does not need the global administrator role.
2707c7tarlx: The recommended access model is **Defender unified RBAC**: it manages the permissions of users and groups for several solutions from a single place (path in the portal: **Permissions > Microsoft Defender XDR > Roles**). It is distinct from Azure RBAC and is configured separately. Points to remember:
1xnbdb8xqp5: - the workloads must be **activated** for the model to apply; as long as a workload is not activated, **the existing access models continue to apply**; Sentinel is activated **per workspace**;
1j2ucpkh0w3: - permissions are grouped: **Security operations** (security data, alerts, response, basic and advanced *live response*, file collection, quarantine and advanced email actions), **Security posture** (posture and vulnerability management) and **Authorization and settings**;
2580ft8qfir: - each role has **assignments**: users or groups, data sources (for example Defender for Endpoint only) and scope;
195h16ogxc6: - Entra roles receive default permissions: *Global administrator* and *Security administrator* have the same; *Global reader* is limited to reading.
ogxp4vtqv0: For Advanced Hunting, the **Security data basics (read)** permission gives access to the alert and behavior tables, but **not** to the email tables: those require **Email & collaboration metadata (read)**. Access to endpoint data follows the Defender for Endpoint RBAC as long as unified RBAC is not activated for that workload.
23rrq0r5748: Microsoft Sentinel is **generally available in the Defender portal**, with or without Defender XDR or an E5 license. The correlation engine then has access to the raw data ingested by Sentinel, which can be found in the Advanced Hunting tables. Defender XDR incidents are visible in Sentinel through the connector, which gives a single main queue; Defender XDR adds its own correlation alerts to the alerts of the Sentinel analytics rules.
10zey6172eo: **Timeline to verify.** The documentation consulted indicates that after **March 31, 2027**, Sentinel will no longer be supported in the Azure portal and will be available only in the Defender portal. An earlier date (July 2026) had been announced then postponed: this is an example of data that changes, hence the consultation date displayed on each source. For new customers since July 2025 who hold the Owner or User Access Administrator role, the workspace is automatically onboarded to the Defender portal.
8sgsuhq8cv: Sentinel does not appear in the list of Defender licenses: its billing model is distinct. Display in the same portal therefore does not include it in your Defender subscription.

For example, Defender for Office 365 is configured in less time than enrolling devices in Defender for Endpoint.
